Investigation: How EU machinery keeps feeding Russian missile makers

Russian metallurgical plants that supply the country’s defense industry during Russia’s war against Ukraine have imported EU-made equipment despite the restrictions aimed at preventing it.

An intermediary, set up in Turkey and owned by a Dutch national, helped supply the banned machinery to Russia, according to customs records obtained by the Kyiv Independent and IrpiMedia.

The records show that the Turkey-based company Redwing Metal shipped $5 million worth of equipment in 2023 and 2024 to two plants in Russia: Aluminum Metallurg Rus (AMR) and Stupino Metallurgical Company (SMK).

Illustration: Nataliia Shulga / The Kyiv Independent.

events.summary: #Ukraine #Russia Intercepting the Ukrainian An-196 Liutyi kamikaze drone presents greater challenges compared to intercepting the Iranian "Geran" (Shahed) drone. The An-196 Liutyi has a cruising speed of approximately 1...
events.raw_text:
#Ukraine #Russia 

Intercepting the Ukrainian An-196 Liutyi kamikaze drone presents greater challenges compared to intercepting the Iranian "Geran" (Shahed) drone. The An-196 Liutyi has a cruising speed of approximately 120–160 km/h, whereas the "Geran" cruises at around 185 km/h. The minimum radial speed for engaged targets by many air defense systems typically ranges from 100–180 km/h. Depending on the target's flight path relative to the air defense system, the radial velocity can be significantly lower than the target's actual airspeed. Consequently, a slow-flying drone such as the Liutyi may be more difficult to detect, track, or engage under certain conditions.

Team Melli’s opener against New Zealand comes just a day after US President Donald Trump said he had reached a deal with the Iranian government, signaling a potential end to the three-and-a-half month conflict.

The cheetahs will also play their first game in Los Angeles, the Californian city nicknamed “Tehrangeles” and home to a largely anti-Iranian government diaspora.

Back in the Middle East, support for the national team, seen by some as representing the government more than the people, is also debatable, especially after the government reportedly killed thousands earlier this year who had taken to the streets in protest.

It’s safe to say, then, that this is an unprecedented situation for any team, and the 11 men on the pitch are caught in the middle.

🎥 Israeli settlers carried out violent arson attacks against Palestinian communities east of Ramallah, torching vehicles, houses and attacking a mosque in the occupied West Bank.

Settlers reportedly set a car on fire, forced their way into a mosque and set it alight, in an attack that residents say could have ended in far greater destruction had locals not intervened.

Palestinian sources reported that an elderly Palestinian man was doused with gasoline during the attack.

The violence continued in nearby Deir Dibwan, where more Palestinian vehicles were burned.

Palestinians and human rights advocates have increasingly described such incidents as pogroms, citing the organised nature of the attacks and their targeting of Palestinian homes, religious sites, property and livelihoods.

Critics argue that years of settler violence, combined with a lack of meaningful accountability, have created an environment in which attacks on Palestinian communities can be carried out repeatedly and with near-total impunity.
